title: break vs continue
idea: Tell break and continue apart by their effect: break ENDS the loop; continue SKIPS one pass. Predict outputs.

exercises.prompt: The big difference: break ___ the loop, continue ___ one pass.
exercises.explanation: break ends the whole loop; continue only skips the current pass and keeps looping.

exercises.prompt: Loop A uses break at i == 3; Loop B uses continue at i == 3, over range(1, 6), printing i otherwise. Which prints MORE numbers?
exercises.explanation: break stops at 3 (prints 1,2). continue skips only 3 (prints 1,2,4,5). B prints more.
break at i == 3 ends the loop after printing 1 and 2.
continue at i == 3 skips only 3, printing 1, 2, 4, 5.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation to the right keyword.
exercises.explanation: Found what you need -> break. Just want to skip some -> continue.

exercises.prompt: After break, the code after the loop runs; after continue, the loop runs its next pass.
exercises.explanation: True - break moves on past the loop; continue moves on to the next pass within the loop.
To stop the whole loop you use break.
To skip one pass and keep going you use continue.

exercises.prompt: Which keyword would make a loop print FEWER total passes of work when a match is common?
exercises.explanation: break ends everything at the first match, so far fewer passes run than continue, which keeps looping.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right tool: 'print all scores except the zeros'.
exercises.explanation: You skip zeros but keep going through the rest, so continue is the fit - break would stop too early.
